entries.reason: Faithful TrustVc port: ALL 17 upstream cases reproduce with the verdict upstream expects (19 TrustVc fns; multi-fn upstream cases keep one TrustVc fn per upstream fn, sharing the upstream_case_id -- the convention the accepted multiset.rs / z3_restart.rs ports use). Four engine features carry the last four cases. (1) PROOF-MODE VARIABLES: inside an `assert .. by` / `assert forall .. by` block Verus coerces every variable read to mode `spec` (vir/src/modes.rs pushes in_forall_stmt for BOTH flavours), and a proof fn's parameters default to spec mode while `tracked` (== `#[verifier::proof]`) makes them proof mode (rust_verify/src/attributes.rs get_var_mode) -- so a `tracked` var CONSUMED by a `tracked` parameter inside a by-block is `expression has mode spec, expected mode proof` (test_assertby1_fail3, test_forallstmt1_fail3), while the same var used in SPEC position is LEGAL (test_forallstmt1's third fn, which VERIFIES). MEASURED before/after: both rejection cases were previously ACCEPTED (Verified) because parse_file_allow_tracked ERASED `tracked`; they now fail closed with the verbatim diagnostic, and the positive counterpart still verifies. (2) The Verus `implies` KEYWORD, whose by-block ASSUMES the antecedent and which emits NO warning, as against `==>`, which assumes nothing and DOES warn. The assumption is confined to the block: the PUBLISHED fact stays the guarded `forall x. A ==> B`, pinned by test_forallstmt2_fails1 (f1(-3) must still be unknown) and by an enclosing-scope leak probe. (3) A VERIFIER-WARNING channel, so test_forallstmt_implies' warning assertion is reproduced and every other case is pinned to ZERO warnings (upstream's default `=> Ok(())` arm asserts warnings.len() == 0). (4) `uninterp spec fn f(x: int) -> bool;` -- a spec fn DECLARED with no body. A bodyless fn parses as syn::Item::Verbatim, so it used to be SILENTLY DROPPED; it is now declared as a symbol that NEVER receives a defining axiom, and no `reveal!` can conjure one because there is no body to reveal (trust-vc-core/tests/uninterp_spec_fn.rs pins that neither p(3) nor !p(3) is provable, with a non-vacuity control that ordinary spec fns still get their axiom). Opaque/reveal, SCOPED reveal inside a by-block, nat binders, block/let/trigger bodies, inferred (untyped) binders, and binders that shadow a parameter all work. test_forallstmt1_fail2's single `// FAILS` obligation is a GENUINE non-proof (constructive non-entailment witness pinned by assert_forall_by_rs_fail2_obligation_is_genuinely_unprovable: f2 = lambda x. x+2 models the post-block hypothesis `forall x. f1(x) > x` yet gives f2(3) == 5 != 4), and its model-less incompleteness Unknown maps to the gate's `counterexample` class (= upstream assert_one_fails, which never inspects a model) exactly as design-unknown-as-failure.md prescribes and as the accepted z3_restart.rs port's test1_fails does. HARNESS-ARTIFACT NOTE (not a replacement gap): upstream test_forallstmt_implies asserts TWO warnings, but only content-checks the first. MEASURED from upstream's own harness (rust_verify_test/tests/common/mod.rs parse_diags): it scoops EVERY rustc JSON diagnostic at level=="warning" into err.warnings, and while it explicitly filters rustc's ERROR summary line (`aborting due to N previous errors`) it has NO equivalent filter for the WARNING summary -- so the second entry is rustc's own `1 warning emitted` emitter summary, not a verifier warning. TrustVc emits the one VERIFIER warning verbatim; it has no rustc emitter to produce a summary counter, and fabricating a second warning to hit a count would be gaming.

entries.reason: TrustVc port: all 7 upstream cases reproduce the matching verifier verdict, with ONE disclosed deviation (test_with_bitvec_nlarith statement-order hoist -- see known_gaps; every obligation is preserved and none weakened, but it is not a byte-order-exact reproduction of the upstream body). Upstream z3_restart.rs is explicitly a mashup of nonlinear.rs, adts_generics.rs, multiset.rs and examples/bitvector_basic.rs, exercised under Verus's z3 spinoff/restart scheduling. Multi-fn upstream cases keep one TrustVc fn per upstream proof/exec fn, all sharing the upstream_case_id (the same convention the accepted multiset.rs port uses). test1_fails and test2_fails are reproduced FAITHFULLY (the previous scout port stood them up as constant-folded assert_by_compute surrogates, and ported test_with_nlarith as a bare assert without the verifier(nonlinear) attribute — those surrogates are gone). test1_fails's single upstream `// FAILS` obligation is a genuine non-proof: pinned by z3_restart_rs_test1_fails_obligation_is_genuinely_false, and its no-model incompleteness failure maps to the gate's `counterexample` (= upstream assert_one_fails, which never inspects a model) exactly as design-unknown-as-failure.md prescribes and as verify.rs implements — mirroring Verus mapping Z3's incompleteness unknown to Invalid(None,None,None).
known_gaps: spinoff_prover is a Verus solver-SCHEDULING knob with no verdict semantics. TrustVc ignores it (mode_attrs.rs) and already discharges each proof obligation as its own solver query, so ignoring it is verdict-equivalent; the port carries the attribute on the same fns upstream does.

DISCLOSED DEVIATION (test_with_bitvec_nlarith): upstream's LITERAL STATEMENT ORDER does not encode. A bit-vector-derived general `&` fact cannot be carried as a hypothesis into a SUBSEQUENT nonlinear-solver query -- the encoder hard-errors with "BitAnd (&) in quantifier body only supports power-of-2 masks". The port therefore HOISTS the trailing `x*y*z == y*x*z` nonlinear by-assert ABOVE the bit-vector by-assert. The body is straight-line pure asserts, so this preserves EVERY obligation, drops none, and gives the hoisted obligation STRICTLY FEWER hypotheses (i.e. it is strictly harder, not weaker). Pinned by three controls in z3_restart_rs_trust_vc_regressions.rs: the hoisted goal verifies standalone; the post-hoist context is not inconsistent (assert(false) still fails, so nothing is vacuously true); and z3_restart_rs_upstream_statement_order_still_hard_errors asserts upstream's literal order STILL fails to encode -- so when that encoder limitation is fixed, that test goes red and forces the port back to upstream order. This is a FAITHFULNESS DEBT, not a soundness one: no obligation is weakened and no false-verify is possible. It is the one respect in which this file is not a byte-order-exact reproduction.

test1_fails's single upstream `// FAILS` obligation is GENUINELY FALSE (in isolation it yields a model-bearing counterexample -- pinned by z3_restart_rs_test1_fails_obligation_is_genuinely_false), but in the full upstream shape the preceding nonlinear product fact pushes its query into the known BV<->Int bridge INCOMPLETENESS, so it returns a MODEL-LESS non-proof. That maps to the gate's `counterexample` label per design-unknown-as-failure.md / verify.rs:660 -- the same mechanism Verus uses when Z3 answers `unknown` (Invalid(None,None,None)); upstream assert_one_fails never inspects a model, and NO model is fabricated. Closing the BV<->Int bridge gap would upgrade this to a model-bearing counterexample.
